comments.author: rwightman
comments.body:
@Nathan33907 first, you're not even using timm here, so wrong library

second there is really not much point in going down this rabbit hole, in timm at least I have made some reasonable efforts to set the seeds correctly, but it's very challenging to have exact reproducibility in most situations as many ops themselves aren't deterministic, or if they can be, will be reduced in performance and require specific overrides to enable. JAX might be a better choice if you are attempting this. Though I have been relatively happy with the reproducibility in timm with defaults, it's not exact but it's pretty consistent run to run with the same seed on most models.

comments.author: Nathan33907
comments.body:
Thank you for your reply. I have solved this problem today.
As for what you said about not using the timm package, that's my mistake. I'm a novice in this field, and I learned that the Tranformers package can be used firstly, so I didn't use the timm package.
I found that using the CPU can reproduce the experiment, while using the GPU requires some improvements to the random number seed setting function. The specific code is as follows:
```python
def set_seed(seed):
    os.environ["CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG"] = ":4096:8"  # control the randomness of cuBLAS
    os.environ["PYTHONHASHSEED"] = str(seed)
    random.seed(seed)
    np.random.seed(seed)
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    torch.cuda.manual_seed(seed)
    torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)
    torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = False
    torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True
    torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)  # force PyTorch to use deterministic algorithms
``` 
The detailed reason is that the parallel softmax/reduction used in self-attention in ViT may have non-determinism, or some parallel architectures of the GPU may cause deviations in floating-point operations. Through the above methods, I was able to reproduce my experiments. However, as you said, there may still be minor differences in each experiment, even though at present, in terms of accuracy and loss, the four decimal places seem reproducible.
Finally, I sincerely thank you again for your reply. At the same time, I hope this post can be helpful to those in need.
Best wishes.
